references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the omer is mentioned as the unit of measure for the manna that the Israelites gathered, providing context for the definition of the omer.
A tenth of an ephah is mentioned as the unit of measure for the sin offering, the same fraction that defines the omer.
A tenth of an ephah is mentioned as the daily grain offering for the priests, the same unit of measure as the omer.
A tenth of an ephah of barley flour is mentioned as an offering, the same fraction that defines the omer.
A tenth of an ephah of fine flour is mentioned as a grain offering, the same unit of measure as the omer.
Ezekiel describes the relationship between the ephah and the homer as standard measures, providing context for biblical units of measurement including the omer.
